answer: Tie each agent to a scarce, attested compute budget: before joining, a node submits a TEE-signed quota proving it holds one real enclave, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand enclaves, not a thousand strings. Reputation then grows only along edges where two agents did verifiable joint work, like surveying a shared meadow of tasks, hauling data across a cedar pipeline, or probing a sparse tundra of cold endpoints. Clones with no attested history and no mutual work stay weightless, so Sybils starve.
